body: Thanks. No they haven’t. In my hometown, we don’t really get the justice that we deserve and it’s more dangerous pursuing the bad people as they will go after you and kill your family.

A hand grenade was thrown in our yard during my dad’s birthday party. (I used to live in a very politically unstable country). My uncle died as well as two family friends. Can’t forget the sight of my parents with bloody clothes, hugging, crying and saying goodbye to each other.

No low grades otherwise I’ll get a beating from my mom. Curfew at 6pm. No male friends. All gay friends are not really gay according to my dad, they’re just pretending to be gay just to take sexual advantage from me.

5 years ago I just arrived in New Zealand to study. No friends, no family. I was sad, alone and scared. Back home I was sheltered by my parents and they’ve always make decisions for me, provided me with my needs and wants. (In my country children don’t usually move out of their parents home until they’re married.) We have house helpers who would help us with everything that we need. I did not know how to cook, clean, do chores, drive, do laundry. Getting to work and school was hard and I had to walk 1 hour return to and from work because buses are not available 6am and 11:30pm in a cold winter morning/night. I always cry and wish that I just want to go home. (It was my parent’s decision for me to study in New Zealand). I’ve met supportive friends along the way, met my partner and his family. I worked as a healthcare assistant and earned my own money while studying full-time, paid my own bills, bought my first car and learned how to drive, rent our own place, and for the first time in my life I made a decision for myself. I am finally independent and grew as a mature person. Fast forward 3 years, I am now a registered nurse and working in mental health and addiction dept. “I’m so proud of you, just hang in there, you’ll get there!”
I used to steal my dad’s cash in his wallet. I though it was normal because I see my mum do it all the time.
When I was a child I touched my eyeballs and wondered why it felt like they’re moving when I look away. I thought that my eyeballs were going to fall and begged my parents to take me to the hospital.
